nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group and let $A$, $B$, $C$ be subgroups of $G$, each abnormal in $G$ and supersoluble, such that $G = AB = BC = CA$ as sets. Then $G$ is supersoluble.
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 19.100 has a positive answer

nodes.summary: The proposition that for every finite group $G$ and all subgroups $A$, $B$, $C$ of $G$ that are abnormal in $G$ and supersoluble, if $G = AB = BC = CA$ as sets, then $G$ is supersoluble.
nodes.title: Abnormal supersoluble trifactorizations (Kourovka 19.100)

nodes.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is abnormal in $G$ if every element $g \in G$ lies in the subgroup generated by $H$ and its conjugate $gHg^{-1}$.
nodes.title: Abnormal subgroup

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is supersoluble if there are a natural number $k$ and subgroups $1 = S_0 \le S_1 \le \cdots \le S_k = G$, each normal in $G$, such that for every $i < k$ we have $S_i \le S_{i+1}$ and there is an element $x \in S_{i+1}$ such that $S_{i+1}$ is generated by $x$ and $S_i$; that is, every factor $S_{i+1}/S_i$ is cyclic.
nodes.title: Supersoluble groups via cyclic normal series
